title: 2022 Year in Review
summary: Four words for the year: searching, sticking with it, finishing what I start, and breaking through
markdown:
Four words for this year: **searching**, **sticking with it**, **finishing what I start**, and **breaking through**.

## Searching

- What do I actually like?
- Who do I want to become?
- What do I want to spend the next years doing?

Only things you like generate the kind of energy that lasts. Coding is still that thing for me — I don't get tired of it.

I also spent the year looking at interesting products and following independent developers. What I want more clearly now is to be someone with solid technical depth *and* room to create.

Over the next few years I'll keep contributing to open source in a sustained way.

## Sticking with it

- Exercise
- Shipping code

As of today I've exercised for 112 days straight — 778 minutes of gym work and 192 km of running this year. Running especially: I can hold 5 km in one go now.

After taking over the company app, I got into the Taro framework, opened discussions around better component type declarations, and so far have submitted 10 PRs (8 merged). I also started the [miniapp-types](https://github.com/robinv8/miniapp-types) project, generating component type schemas from the various mini-program docs.

## Finishing what I start

- Fixing umijs SSR performance
- Polishing the app
- Shipping CanIUse

The SegmentFault community main site frontend depended on umijs. SSR was eating too much memory, and official SSR maintenance was fading, so we had to move. We chose Next.js. After about half a year of work, the main site is rebuilt on Next.js — server memory roughly halved — and it's in canary now.

The community app wasn't originally my job, but the native app was no longer maintainable. A colleague and I took on the rewrite: I owned the framework and base features; he owned business features. When we hit ~90%, I ran out of bandwidth. Lately I've been using off-hours to finish the remaining work so we can ship sooner.

CanIUse came from Zakary, a Taro core member — mini-program components have a lot of props, and we wanted a CanIUse-style check. It shipped.

## Breaking through

From searching, to sticking with it, to finishing things — and then the bottleneck gave. A lot landed this year.

1. Became a Taro collaborator and joined the Taro technical committee
1. Created two open-source projects:
   - https://github.com/robinv8/miniapp-types
   - https://github.com/robinv8/daily

## Closing

2022 was a rough year for the industry at large. That doesn't mean the mind has to follow. 2023 is the year I turn thirty — may everything keep getting better.
